status: literature values, NOT calibrated for Jakarta. Run sensitivity (low and high) before any quantitative use.
how_used: Cell value = mean of the class n over the WorldCover 10 m pixels inside the model cell. Face value = mean of the two neighbouring cell values (same as SFINCS).

10.label: Tree cover
10.basis: HEC-RAS Table 3-1 / Chow (1959) floodplain trees and brush, medium of the plugin table

20.label: Shrubland
20.basis: HEC-RAS Table 3-1 / Chow (1959) medium to dense brush

30.label: Grassland
30.basis: HEC-RAS Table 3-1 / Chow (1959) pasture, short and high grass

40.label: Cropland
40.basis: HEC-RAS Table 3-1 / Chow (1959) mature row crops

50.label: Built-up
50.basis: Bare-earth DEM (FABDEM removes buildings), so buildings act through an increased effective roughness; Beretta et al. (2018, doi:10.3390/geosciences8020077) found an adjusted roughness about as accurate as explicit building geometry in a laboratory urban district. Typical 0.15; low 0.12 and high 0.20 are the HEC-RAS 2D land-classification range for Developed, High Intensity (after Chow 1959). HEC-RAS notes that these values are for appreciable depths and shallow overland flow needs higher values. NOT the plugin value 0.018 (a smooth constructed channel).

60.label: Bare / sparse vegetation
60.basis: NRCS Ch. 15 Table 15-1 smooth surface 0.011, HEC-RAS barren land 0.023 to 0.030

80.label: Permanent water bodies
80.basis: HEC-RAS land classification open water 0.025 to 0.05; Chow clean winding channel

90.label: Herbaceous wetland
90.basis: HEC-RAS emergent herbaceous wetlands 0.05 to 0.085; USGS WSP 2339 vegetation adjustment

95.label: Mangroves
95.basis: USGS WSP 2339 dense woody vegetation (plugin value, not used in the Jakarta sample)
